marker: # ref_size is the product length measured in the LVS assembly GCA_000009245.1 (AM233362.1) by in silico
# PCR with these primers, outer primer edge to outer primer edge. Every marker gives exactly one product.
# THE SOURCE TABLE GIVES PRIMERS ONLY. Ten of the eleven loci are now callable and one is not. The unit
# and the copy number of ten loci are taken from the bundled scheme francisella_johansson_2004, which
# counts the same arrays, now that that scheme carries the published copy numbers of Johansson et al.
# 2004 Table 2. The eleventh, Ft-M20B, has a published unit but no published count.
# The unit of the ten rests on two lines of evidence that agree: a cross strain test, in which a locus
# keeps one flanking length so its product sizes differ by whole multiples of the unit, over seven
# Francisella genomes, SCHU S4, LVS, OSU18, WY96-3418, FSC198, NE061598 and TI0902; and the unit the
# Johansson scheme records for the same locus. The copy number comes from calibrating through SCHU S4:
# the array a locus contains is the same DNA whichever primers flank it, so this scheme's SCHU S4
# product minus the array the Johansson scheme counts there gives this scheme's flank, which fixes the
# copy number in LVS.
#   locus    Johansson locus, unit and SCHU S4 count   flank   LVS count
#   Ft-M02   Ft-M2    6 bp   4 copies                    327     2
#   Ft-M03   Ft-M3    9 bp  25 copies                    209    16
#   Ft-M04   Ft-M4    5 bp   3 copies                    202     4
#   Ft-M05   Ft-M5   16 bp   3 copies                    268     2
#   Ft-M06   Ft-M6   21 bp   4 copies                    188     4
#   Ft-M10   Ft-M10  16 bp  18 copies                    166     2
#   Ft-M20A  Ft-M20  12 bp   3 copies                    271     4
#   Ft-M22   Ft-M22   6 bp   2 copies                    154     4
#   Ft-M23   Ft-M23  23 bp   2 copies                    304     1
#   Ft-M24   Ft-M24  21 bp   1 copy                      375     2
# The calibration passes two checks. Every flank yields a whole number of repeats in LVS, which a wrong
# unit or pairing would not. And because both schemes count the same array, their alleles agree for any
# strain: across the genomes where both panels amplify, every locus and strain pair gives the same
# allele. The scale is therefore the published Johansson one, and the two Francisella schemes are now
# consistent with each other. A few loci give a fractional allele in some lineages, from a flank indel
# or the shared repeat family, and those are flagged INTERMEDIATE rather than rounded; the reference
# call is a whole number at every locus.
# Ft-M20B is the one locus left uncallable. Vogler et al. split the Johansson Ft-M20 locus into Ft-M20A,
# the originally described 12 bp repeat, and Ft-M20B, a roughly 200 bp insertion carrying a separate
# 15 bp repeat. The 15 bp unit is published (Vogler et al. 2008), and it is recorded here, but no
# publication gives its copy number, and the insertion is monomorphic at 153 bp in subspecies
# holarctica, which LVS belongs to, so the reference array is a single faint copy that cannot be pinned
# to an absolute count. It is diverse only in subspecies tularensis. The locus is therefore sized with
# its published unit but not called.
# THE LOCUS NAMES OF THE TWO SCHEMES DIFFER ONLY IN SPELLING. This scheme pads the number, Ft-M02,
# where francisella_johansson_2004 does not, Ft-M2, and the agreement above confirms the padded and
# unpadded names are the same VNTR. Ft-M20 there is split here into Ft-M20A and Ft-M20B. The two still
# amplify different fragments, so their product sizes are not comparable even though their alleles are.
